title: マイクロソフト、AI機能を強化した新ハードとWindowsの変更を発表
title_zh: 微软发布新款AI硬件，Windows也要大改版
lead: マイクロソフトは2年ぶりとなるリアルイベントを開催し、新しいSurfaceノートPCやWindows 11の変更点を発表した。ローカルAIとエージェント型ワークフローが、個人向けコンピューティングをどう変えるかという構想も示された。
lead_zh: 微软时隔两年举办线下发布会，公布了新款Surface笔记本以及Windows 11的一系列改动，还展示了本地AI和智能体工作流将如何改变个人计算的构想。

paragraphs: マイクロソフトは、2年ぶりとなるライブイベントで新型「Surface Laptop Ultra」を発表した。同社が2026年5月に予告していた製品で、新しいNvidia RTX Spark SoCを採用する初のモデルである。価格は2,599ドルからで、SoCとメモリの構成は複数用意され、5120コアまたは6144コアのBlackwell GPUと最大128GBのLPDDR5x統合メモリを搭載する。10月16日に出荷を開始し、現在予約を受け付けている。

発表では、開発者向けの「Surface RTX Spark Dev Box」も公開された。Nvidiaのジェンスン・フアン氏とマイクロソフトCEOのサティア・ナデラ氏が登壇し、Windows部門社長のパヴァン・ダヴルリ氏が説明した。価格は5,999ドルで、AI開発に最適化したWindows 11を搭載し、128GBの統合メモリとRTX GPUにより1ペタフロップスのAI演算性能を実現するとしている。筐体には1,000個の通気口があり、1,000テラフロップスにちなんだ設計だ。

ソフトウェア面では、Windows 11のCopilotが大幅に刷新される。新しい画面は「Home」「Code」「Autopilot」の3つのタブに分かれ、プログラミング経験のない利用者でもウィジェットやアプリを開発できるとされる。また、検索バーからシステム設定を直接実行できる新機能や、エージェントの活動をサンドボックスに閉じ込めるセキュリティ枠組み「Microsoft Execution Containers（MXC）」も発表された。

マイクロソフトはこれらの取り組みを「Hybrid Intelligence」と呼び、クラウド依存からローカルAIへの移行を目指す。Surface Laptop UltraとRTX Spark Dev Boxの利用者は、用途に応じてメモリを自由に割り当てられ、llama.cppやDeepseek、Nvidia Nemotron系のモデルをネイティブに扱える。同社はローカルAIに大きく賭けているが、セキュリティや利用者の受け入れをめぐる疑問は残っている。
paragraphs_zh: 微软在时隔两年的线下发布会上推出了新款“Surface Laptop Ultra”。这款产品早在2026年5月就做过预告，是首款采用英伟达RTX Spark系统级芯片的机型。起售价2,599美元，提供多种芯片和内存配置，搭载5120核或6144核的Blackwell GPU，以及最高128GB的LPDDR5x统一内存。10月16日开始发货，目前已经可以预订。

发布会上还公开了面向开发者的“Surface RTX Spark Dev Box”。英伟达的黄仁勋和微软CEO萨提亚·纳德拉登台，Windows与设备部门总裁帕万·达武鲁里做了介绍。该设备售价5,999美元，预装针对AI开发优化的Windows 11，凭借128GB统一内存和板载RTX GPU，号称可实现1千万亿次浮点运算的AI算力。机身设有1000个通风口，设计上呼应了1000万亿次运算这一数字。
软件方面，Windows 11内置的Copilot将大幅改版。新界面分为“Home”“Code”“Autopilot”三个标签页，微软称即使没有编程经验的人也能开发小组件和应用。此外，微软还发布了可直接从搜索栏执行系统设置的新功能，以及把智能体活动限制在沙箱内的安全框架“Microsoft Execution Containers（MXC）”。
微软将这一系列举措称为“Hybrid Intelligence”，意在从依赖云端转向本地AI。Surface Laptop Ultra和RTX Spark Dev Box的用户可以按用途自由分配内存，并原生支持llama.cpp以及Deepseek、英伟达Nemotron系列模型。微软在本地AI上押下重注，但围绕安全性和用户接受度的疑问依然存在。

In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts.
Surface Laptop Ultra
Originally teased in May 2026
, the new Surface Laptop Ultra will be Microsoft’s first offering to take advantage of the new Nvidia RTX Spark SoC (system on a chip). The device has a starting price of $2,599, and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for
pre-order
now.
While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment. The new
Gears of War: E-Day
was shown running on the system, meaning that even without a traditional gaming GPU, AAA titles are on the table.
RTX Spark Dev Box
Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the
Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.
This is a $5,999 anodized aluminum black box “designed to meet the needs of frontier developers.” The Spark Dev Box ships with a custom “developer-optimized” build of Windows 11 pre-configured for AI development and local AI use. With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance.
The RTX Spark Dev Box’s design is quite sleek. The unit physically resembles something like an Android TV box or game console more than it does a traditional PC. In fact, the vent pattern on the top of the unit is reminiscent of what you see looking down at the top of an Xbox Series X. According to Microsoft’s provided press materials, the venting on the RTX Spark Dev box has 1,000 chassis air vents as a nod to the 1,000 teraflops of AI performance.
Local agentic AI is coming to Windows
Outside of the hardware announcements, Microsoft outlined a host of changes headed for Windows 11 this fall. OS builds featured on the Surface Ultra and Spark Box will arrive with an updated Windows software suite to support local model testing out of the box.
Copilot overhaul
Microsoft’s baked-in Windows AI, Copilot, is getting a major overhaul. The new Copilot layout will see things divided into three tabs:
Home
– A starting place where users can interact with LLM models
Code
– The space where Microsoft claims that users with no previous coding experience will be able to prompt their way to developing widgets and Windows applications.
Autopilot
– The tab for interacting with AI agents. This is where users will oversee their agentic bot tasks.
New Windows Search Experience
Coming to a Windows PC later this year, the new update will allow Windows users to execute system-level tasks directly from the search bar. Rather than opening up something like Control Panel to adjust display settings, the user will presumably be able to describe the action they want and have the system execute it directly from the taskbar tray.
Microsoft Execution Containers
For those who might still feel a little trepidation about turning over their entire digital lives and files to AI bots, Microsoft announced the availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a security framework designed to keep agent activities confined to a sandbox. Available to developers today, the framework allows system admins and organizations to monitor active agents working within their systems and to specifically set guardrails for each, ensuring control over exactly what each agent is able to access.
MXC acts as a policy layer
that directs compute traffic to the appropriate isolation backend. Depending on the workload, MXC can shift to a process container, session container, WSL container, or even an experimental hardware-backed isolation called MicroVM.
The hybrid approach
Bringing all of this new agentic workflow together with traditional Windows is a concept that Microsoft calls “Hybrid Intelligence,” which is a move away from cloud-backed AI solutions and a move toward local ones. Hybrid Intelligence will allow Surface Laptop Ultra or RTX Spark Dev Box users to allocate memory as they see fit for any specific application, as well as offer native support for local frameworks like
llama.cpp
and models from the
Deepseek
and
Nvidia Nemotron
families.
We’ll see if it works soon enough
Microsoft is betting big on local AI with the changes announced today, but questions about security and user acceptance still remain, especially in light of their past missteps and other
recent AI agent mishaps
. The Surface Laptop Ultra hits shelves next week—keep an eye out for our review, and we’ll try to figure out whether it’s worth the $2,599 entry price and what this local AI capability buys you.
